A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEACE-based document-embedding study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–H support comparison despite the changed title and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering, document-retrieval, multilingual similarity, bitext-mining, and supplementary analysis results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports unsuccessful exploration of automatically generated features.

M1.justification: Both versions fit and apply the same closed-form LEACE affine transformation to pretrained embeddings using confounder labels. The newly advertised wrapper and revised mathematical exposition do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains CAP source combinations, SCOTUS summaries, SemEval news, German/French/Italian Swiss summaries, MTEB retrieval and similarity tasks, and bitext mining. No additional dataset, language, or task coverage is identified.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments, including original embeddings and the PC1-removal baseline in Appendix E. The embedding-model sets are retained; newly cited unsupervised methods are not reported as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset counts, construction using up to 1,024 document pairs, k=21 clustering, evaluation metrics, and model–eraser combinations are retained. The new automatic-feature exploration does not specify a distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v3 newly reports an exploration of automatic feature generation to address reliance on supplied labels, without downstream improvements or detailed analysis. Existing PCA comparisons, cluster-count sensitivity, and legal case studies remain; moving qualitative discussion from Appendix F to Section 4.2.1 is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies additional run counts, seeds, or uncertainty procedures. Point-estimate tables and the PC1 correlation analysis retain the same reporting, including r=0.79 and p<0.001.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–11 are unchanged. The introduction merely rounds 0.175→0.826 to 0.18→0.83, and new Figure 2 redisplays existing scores. The added result is the qualitative report that automatic feature generation produced no measurable downstream improvement.

T1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises the central derivation: v1’s three-term expected-similarity expression becomes a pairwise expansion including cross terms; v3 explicitly assumes IID document draws, changes the distortion objective to squared norm, and rewrites the projected-loading and noise decomposition. These alter mathematical reasoning beyond notation, although the LEACE map is retained.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a practical contribution through the announced encoding/erasure wrapper and released labeled evaluation resources. The central claims of improved clustering and retrieval, low computational cost, and preserved out-of-distribution performance remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits usefulness when relevance depends on higher-order discourse features such as blended facts, judgments, and framing. Its limitations also discuss unsuccessful automatic features and possible unsupervised or expert-validated alternatives. The earlier limitations concerning numerous source categories and mixed multilingual-retrieval findings remain.

D1.justification: v1 lists a code repository while also promising later data/code release; v3 states that code and data are available at an updated repository address and describes a convenience wrapper. The PCA caption newly identifies multilingual E5. These are access and documentation changes, not established experimental changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Fan et al. (2025) to the legal discussion and Kim, Seo, Yang, Movva, and Paulo references concerning unsupervised debiasing or interpretable features. Established LEACE positioning remains. Replacing the MTEB preprint citation with its publication does not introduce a different work.

P1.justification: There is extensive prose revision across the Introduction, Background, Sections 5–6, Conclusion, and Limitations. Qualitative interpretation moves from Appendix F into new Section 4.2.1, while the retained examples receive separate appendix subsections. The title, author information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds an E5-base overview chart as Figure 2 using existing results. Retained charts are resized or repositioned, and tables receive revised emphasis and captions. These are limited display changes rather than a replacement of the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The reported wrapper/data release, overview figure, more prominent qualitative discussion, and more explicit limitations improve usability and interpretation. The mathematical revision repairs some omissions, but v3 Equation 9 still incorrectly adds a vector noise term to scalar similarity. With benchmark evidence unchanged and the derivation only partly repaired, the overall improvement is limited.
